traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Caricaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple or compound; compound leaves palmate; veins usually palmate, rarely pinnate; stipules usually absent, sometimes present; plants usually polygamous, sometimes monoecious or dioecious; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit berry; parts of each whorl 5; stamens 5 to 10; carpels 5. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.flowering_position.note: APweb, Brassicales page, Caricaceae (read 2026-10-16): axillary cymose inflorescences.
